sights.n: Cincinnati Museum Center at Union Terminal
sights.w: One of the last grand Art Deco railroad terminals (1933), a National Historic Landmark whose half-dome rotunda now houses the History, Natural History & Science, and Children's museums plus an OMNIMAX theater.
sights.k: Multi-museum complex; check which museums/exhibits are open before visiting.

sights.address: 100 W Mehring Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202 (Covington side: 200 Riverside Dr, Covington, KY 41011)
sights.w: Opened 1867 as the longest suspension span in the world, John A. Roebling's Ohio River bridge was the prototype for his Brooklyn Bridge; its illuminated cables are Cincinnati's signature riverfront image.

sights.n: Fountain Square & the Tyler Davidson Fountain
sights.w: The city's civic living room since 1871, anchored by 'The Genius of Water,' Ferdinand von Miller's bronze fountain gifted by Henry Probasco in memory of Tyler Davidson.
The 49th-floor open-air deck atop the 1931 Art Deco Carew Tower (by the Empire State Building's architects) long gave the best downtown-and-river panorama.
sights.k: Deck closed as of 2026 during the tower's conversion to apartments; slated to reopen but no date announced. The building's ground-floor Art Deco arcade remains accessible.

sights.w: Samuel Hannaford's 1878 High Victorian Gothic landmark facing Washington Park, home to the Cincinnati Symphony, Pops, Opera and Ballet, reopened in 2017 after a $143M restoration.
Opened 2004 on the riverfront where escaping slaves crossed the Ohio, this museum tells the story of the Underground Railroad and contemporary freedom struggles, anchored by a rescued slave pen.
The nation's second-oldest zoo (1875) and an accredited botanical garden, now world-famous as the home of Fiona the hippo, born prematurely in 2017.
Ohio's oldest continuously operated public market (1855), an iron-framed OTR institution packed with Eckerlin Meats, Pho Lang Thang and dozens of vendors plus a weekend farmers' market.
A restored 6-acre park (reopened 2012) across from Music Hall with an interactive fountain, bandstand and event lawn, the green heart of Over-the-Rhine's revival.

sights.n: Great American Ball Park & Reds Hall of Fame
sights.w: Riverfront home of the Cincinnati Reds, baseball's oldest professional franchise, since 2003; the adjoining Reds Hall of Fame & Museum honors the Big Red Machine.
The riverfront home of the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals since 2000 (formerly Paul Brown Stadium), part of the downtown sports-and-Banks corridor.
FC Cincinnati's $250M soccer-specific stadium in the West End, opened 2021, known for a translucent LED-lit facade and one of MLS's loudest atmospheres.

sights.n: Smale Riverfront Park & Carol Ann's Carousel
sights.w: A landscaped riverfront park between the ballpark and stadium with swings, water features and Carol Ann's Carousel, whose 44 hand-carved animals honor Cincinnati history.

sights.address: 705 E Pete Rose Way, Cincinnati, OH 45202
sights.w: A mile of riverfront park at Yeatman's Cove where the stepped Serpentine Wall (1976) descends to the Ohio, a classic spot to sit and watch the river and the Kentucky skyline.
A 2,670-ft former rail bridge, restored in 2006 as a purple-painted pedestrian-only crossing linking Newport on the Levee to downtown Cincinnati with skyline views.
A riverfront aquarium at Newport on the Levee with 20,000+ animals, walk-through acrylic tunnels and a rope 'Shark Bridge' suspended over the sharks.

sights.address: Main St & W 6th St, Covington, KY 41011
sights.w: A restored 19th-century German neighborhood in Covington with Italianate storefronts, bars and the Carroll Chimes Bell Tower's animated Pied Piper show over the Goose Girl Fountain.
The Drees Pavilion overlook in Covington's 700-acre Devou Park frames the definitive postcard view of the Cincinnati skyline across the Ohio, renovated in 2024.

sights.address: Vine St & E 12th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202
sights.w: One of the largest, most intact urban historic districts in the U.S. (NRHP 1983, ~943 contributing buildings) with the country's largest contiguous collection of 19th-century Italianate architecture, built by German immigrants.
Long-running Ohio River sightseeing, lunch and dinner cruises departing the Newport landing on Riverboat Row, across from downtown Cincinnati.
sights.k: Regular sightseeing schedule runs roughly Memorial Day to Labor Day; check dates.

sights.w: A multi-level riverfront dining and entertainment complex (opened 2001) housing the Newport Aquarium, a food hall, cinema and comedy club, at the foot of the Purple People Bridge.
An 18-acre mixed-use riverfront district tucked between the ballpark and Paycor Stadium, tying together restaurants, bars and residences alongside Smale Park and the Freedom Center.
